functional.title: Verify all primary UI components render correctly on initial page load
preconditions: User is authenticated and logged into the application with a valid session
The application is deployed to the test environment with the latest build containing UI component changes
Browser is a supported version (Chrome 120+, Firefox 115+, Safari 17+, Edge 120+)
Network connectivity is stable with no throttling applied

steps.action: Navigate to the main application URL and wait for the page to fully load
steps.expectedResult: The page loads within 3 seconds, all primary UI components (header, navigation, main content area, footer) are visible without layout shifts or broken elements

steps.action: Inspect the header section for logo, navigation menu items, and user profile icon
steps.expectedResult: Header displays the application logo on the left, navigation menu items are horizontally aligned, and the user profile avatar/icon appears on the right side of the header

steps.action: Inspect the main content area for all expected UI widgets, cards, or data display components
steps.expectedResult: All UI components render with correct styling, proper spacing, consistent font sizes, and no overlapping elements. Placeholder or loading states are shown for data-dependent components

steps.action: Scroll down the page to verify all below-the-fold components render correctly
steps.expectedResult: All components below the fold render as the user scrolls, with smooth scrolling behavior and no flickering or layout jumps

steps.action: Resize the browser window to 1024x768 resolution
steps.expectedResult: All UI components adapt responsively, maintaining readability and usability without horizontal scrollbars or content overflow

steps.action: Resize the browser window to 375x667 (mobile viewport)
steps.expectedResult: Components stack vertically in a mobile-friendly layout, navigation collapses into a hamburger menu, and all interactive elements remain tappable with adequate touch target sizes (minimum 44x44px)

postconditions: All UI components are rendered correctly across tested viewport sizes
No JavaScript console errors related to component rendering are present
User remains authenticated and on the correct page

functional.title: Verify navigation between UI components and page routing works correctly
preconditions: User is logged in with standard user role permissions
Application is fully loaded on the main dashboard/landing page
Browser history is clear to ensure clean navigation state

steps.action: Click on the first navigation menu item in the top navigation bar
steps.expectedResult: The application navigates to the corresponding page/view, the URL updates to reflect the new route, and the clicked menu item shows an active/selected state (highlighted or underlined)

steps.action: Click on the second navigation menu item
steps.expectedResult: The application transitions smoothly to the second page/view without a full page reload, the URL updates, and the previously active menu item loses its active state while the new one gains it

steps.action: Click the browser's Back button
steps.expectedResult: The application navigates back to the first page/view, the URL reverts, and the correct menu item shows the active state

steps.action: Click the browser's Forward button
steps.expectedResult: The application navigates forward to the second page/view, maintaining all previously loaded state and data

steps.action: Click on the application logo in the header
steps.expectedResult: The application navigates back to the main dashboard/home page

steps.action: Manually type a valid application route in the browser address bar and press Enter
steps.expectedResult: The application loads the correct page for the manually entered route with all components properly initialized

postconditions: Browser history contains all navigated routes in correct order
No broken links or 404 errors encountered during navigation
User session remains active throughout all navigation actions

functional.title: Verify form UI components accept valid input and submit data successfully
preconditions: User is logged in with permissions to create/edit data
User has navigated to a page containing a form with input fields (text, dropdown, date picker, checkbox, etc.)
No pre-existing validation errors are displayed on the form
Backend API services are running and accessible

steps.action: Click on the first text input field and enter a valid value such as 'Test Component Name'
steps.expectedResult: The text input field accepts the typed value, displays it correctly, and shows no validation error. The field border may change to indicate focus state (e.g., blue border)

steps.action: Click on a dropdown/select component and select an option from the list
steps.expectedResult: The dropdown opens showing all available options, the selected option is highlighted, and upon selection the dropdown closes displaying the chosen value

steps.action: Click on a date picker component and select a valid date (e.g., today's date)
steps.expectedResult: The date picker calendar opens, today's date is highlighted, clicking the date populates the field with the formatted date (e.g., 'MM/DD/YYYY'), and the calendar closes

steps.action: Toggle a checkbox or switch component to the 'on' state
steps.expectedResult: The checkbox shows a checkmark or the toggle switch slides to the 'on' position with appropriate visual feedback (color change, animation)

steps.action: Fill in all remaining required fields with valid data
steps.expectedResult: All required fields are populated, no validation errors are shown, and the 'Submit' or 'Save' button becomes enabled (if it was previously disabled)

steps.action: Click the 'Submit' or 'Save' button
steps.expectedResult: A loading indicator appears on the button or form, the form data is submitted to the backend API, and a success notification/toast message appears (e.g., 'Data saved successfully' in a green banner)

steps.action: Verify the submitted data appears in the corresponding list or detail view
steps.expectedResult: The newly submitted data is visible in the data list/table or detail view with all field values matching what was entered

postconditions: Data is persisted in the backend database with correct field values
Success notification was displayed and auto-dismissed after a few seconds
User is redirected to the appropriate page (list view or confirmation page)
Form fields are cleared or the form is no longer in edit mode

functional.title: Verify data integration - UI components correctly fetch and display data from backend API
preconditions: User is authenticated with valid credentials and appropriate role
Backend API is running and contains at least 5 records of test data
Network DevTools panel is open to monitor API calls
Application is on the main page before navigating to the data view

steps.action: Navigate to the page/view that displays data fetched from the backend API (e.g., a data table, list, or dashboard widget)
steps.expectedResult: A loading spinner or skeleton loader is displayed while data is being fetched from the API

steps.action: Wait for the data to load completely and observe the UI components
steps.expectedResult: The loading indicator disappears and is replaced by the actual data. The data table/list shows records with correct column headers and properly formatted data values

steps.action: Verify the number of records displayed matches the expected count from the API response (check Network tab)
steps.expectedResult: The number of rows/items displayed in the UI matches the total count returned by the API. If pagination is present, the total count indicator shows the correct number

steps.action: Compare at least 3 individual data records between the UI display and the raw API response in the Network tab
steps.expectedResult: All field values (names, dates, numbers, statuses) displayed in the UI exactly match the corresponding values in the API JSON response, with proper formatting applied (e.g., dates formatted, currency symbols added)

steps.action: Click on a specific record/row to view its detail page or expanded view
steps.expectedResult: The detail view opens showing all fields for the selected record, including any additional fields not shown in the list view. An additional API call may be made for detailed data

steps.action: Verify the API request headers include proper authentication tokens (check Network tab)
steps.expectedResult: The API request includes an Authorization header with a valid Bearer token, and the Content-Type header is set to 'application/json'

postconditions: All data displayed in UI components accurately reflects the backend data
No data transformation errors or missing fields observed
API calls completed with 200 status codes and appropriate response times (under 2 seconds)

functional.title: Verify interactive UI components - buttons, modals, tooltips, and action menus function correctly
preconditions: User is logged in and on a page containing interactive UI components
Page has fully loaded with no pending API calls
At least one data record exists for interaction testing

steps.action: Hover over a button component (e.g., 'Add New', 'Edit', or 'Delete')
steps.expectedResult: The button shows a hover state with visual feedback (color change, shadow, cursor changes to pointer). If a tooltip is configured, it appears after a brief delay showing descriptive text

steps.action: Click the 'Add New' or equivalent primary action button
steps.expectedResult: A modal dialog or new form view opens with a smooth animation. The modal has a clear title, form fields, and action buttons ('Save'/'Cancel'). The background is dimmed with an overlay

steps.action: Click the 'Cancel' button or the 'X' close icon on the modal
steps.expectedResult: The modal closes with a smooth animation, the background overlay is removed, and no data changes are made. Focus returns to the element that triggered the modal

steps.action: Right-click or click the three-dot menu (kebab menu) on a data record row
steps.expectedResult: A context menu or action dropdown appears with options such as 'View', 'Edit', 'Delete', 'Duplicate'. Menu items are clearly labeled with appropriate icons

steps.action: Click outside the action menu to dismiss it
steps.expectedResult: The action menu closes and no action is performed

steps.action: Hover over an element that has a tooltip (e.g., an info icon or truncated text)
steps.expectedResult: A tooltip appears within 300ms showing the full text or helpful information. The tooltip is positioned correctly (not clipped by viewport edges) and disappears when the mouse moves away

postconditions: All interactive components return to their default state after interaction
No unintended side effects or data modifications occurred
UI remains responsive and functional after multiple interactions

functional.title: Verify search, filter, and sort functionality on data display components
preconditions: User is logged in and on a page with a data table or list component
At least 10 data records exist with varied values for testing search, filter, and sort
Search bar, filter controls, and sortable column headers are visible

steps.action: Click on the search input field and type a known value that exists in the data (e.g., 'Alpha Project')
steps.expectedResult: The data list/table filters in real-time (or after pressing Enter) to show only records matching the search term. A result count indicator updates to reflect the filtered number of records

steps.action: Clear the search field by clicking the 'X' clear button or selecting all text and deleting
steps.expectedResult: The full unfiltered dataset is restored and displayed. The result count returns to the original total

steps.action: Click on a filter dropdown (e.g., 'Status') and select a specific filter value (e.g., 'Active')
steps.expectedResult: The data list updates to show only records matching the selected filter. A filter tag/chip appears indicating the active filter. Records not matching the filter are hidden

steps.action: Click on a sortable column header (e.g., 'Name' or 'Date Created')
steps.expectedResult: The data is sorted in ascending order by the clicked column. A sort indicator arrow (▲) appears next to the column header

steps.action: Click the same column header again
steps.expectedResult: The sort order toggles to descending. The sort indicator arrow changes direction (▼). Data is reordered accordingly

steps.action: Apply a filter and a search term simultaneously
steps.expectedResult: Both filter and search criteria are applied together (AND logic). Only records matching both the filter value and search term are displayed

steps.action: Click a 'Clear All Filters' or 'Reset' button if available
steps.expectedResult: All active filters, search terms, and sort orders are cleared. The data returns to its default unfiltered, unsorted state

postconditions: Data display returns to default state after clearing all filters
No data was modified during search, filter, or sort operations
Performance remained acceptable (results updated within 1 second)

functional.title: Verify UI components handle loading states and empty states gracefully
preconditions: User is authenticated and has access to the application
Test environment can be configured to simulate slow API responses or empty datasets
Browser DevTools Network tab is accessible for throttling

steps.action: Open browser DevTools, go to Network tab, and set throttling to 'Slow 3G' to simulate slow network
steps.expectedResult: Network throttling is applied successfully

steps.action: Navigate to a page that fetches data from the backend API
steps.expectedResult: Loading indicators (spinners, skeleton loaders, or progress bars) are displayed in place of data components while the API call is in progress. The UI does not show broken layouts or raw JSON

steps.action: Wait for the data to eventually load
steps.expectedResult: Loading indicators are replaced by actual data components once the API response is received. The transition is smooth without layout shifts

steps.action: Remove network throttling and navigate to a view/page where no data records exist (empty dataset)
steps.expectedResult: An empty state illustration or message is displayed (e.g., 'No records found' with an icon). A call-to-action button such as 'Create your first record' may be present

steps.action: If a 'Create your first record' or similar CTA button is present, click it
steps.expectedResult: The application navigates to the creation form or opens a modal to add a new record

postconditions: Loading states were displayed appropriately during data fetching
Empty states provided clear messaging and actionable next steps
No unhandled errors or broken UI elements observed

functional.title: Verify UI component state persistence across page refresh and browser session
preconditions: User is logged in with an active session
User has made some UI state changes (e.g., selected filters, toggled settings, expanded sections)
Application supports state persistence via URL parameters, local storage, or session storage

steps.action: Apply a filter on a data table (e.g., select 'Status: Active') and note the current URL
steps.expectedResult: The filter is applied and the URL may update with query parameters reflecting the filter state (e.g., '?status=active')

steps.action: Press F5 or click the browser refresh button to reload the page
steps.expectedResult: After page reload, the previously applied filter is still active. The data table shows the same filtered results. The filter UI control shows the selected filter value

steps.action: Copy the current URL with filter parameters and open it in a new browser tab
steps.expectedResult: The new tab loads the page with the same filter applied, showing identical filtered results

steps.action: Navigate away from the page to a different section of the application, then navigate back using the browser Back button
steps.expectedResult: The page loads with the previously applied UI state (filters, sort order, scroll position if applicable)

steps.action: Check browser local storage or session storage in DevTools for any persisted UI state
steps.expectedResult: Relevant UI state data is stored in local/session storage with appropriate keys and valid JSON values

postconditions: UI state is correctly persisted and restored across page refreshes
Shareable URLs with state parameters work correctly in new tabs
No stale or corrupted state data in browser storage

functional.title: Verify UI components render correctly with different user roles and permissions
preconditions: Test accounts exist for at least two different roles: Admin and Standard User (or Viewer)
Role-based access control is configured in the backend
Both accounts have valid credentials and active sessions available

steps.action: Log in with the Admin role account and navigate to the main application page
steps.expectedResult: All UI components are visible including admin-specific elements such as 'Settings', 'User Management', 'Delete' buttons, and configuration panels

steps.action: Verify that action buttons like 'Create', 'Edit', 'Delete' are visible and enabled for the Admin user
steps.expectedResult: All CRUD action buttons are present, enabled, and clickable. Admin-only menu items appear in the navigation

steps.action: Log out of the Admin account
steps.expectedResult: User is logged out and redirected to the login page

steps.action: Log in with the Standard User (or Viewer) role account and navigate to the same page
steps.expectedResult: The page loads but admin-specific UI components are hidden or disabled. For example, 'Delete' buttons may be absent, 'Settings' menu item may not appear, and 'Edit' buttons may be replaced with 'View' buttons

steps.action: Attempt to access an admin-only page by directly entering its URL in the browser address bar
steps.expectedResult: The application either redirects the user to an 'Access Denied' page with a clear message, or redirects to the dashboard with an error notification such as 'You do not have permission to access this page'

steps.action: Verify that data visible to the Standard User is appropriately scoped (e.g., only their own records or public records)
steps.expectedResult: The data displayed is limited to what the Standard User role is authorized to see. No admin-only or restricted data is visible

postconditions: Admin UI components are only visible to Admin role users
Standard Users cannot access restricted pages or actions
Role-based rendering is consistent across all pages and components

functional.title: Verify real-time data updates and component refresh behavior
preconditions: User is logged in and viewing a data display component (table/list/dashboard)
A second browser session or API tool (e.g., Postman) is available to modify backend data
The application supports real-time updates via WebSocket, polling, or manual refresh

steps.action: Note the current data displayed in the UI component (record count and specific values)
steps.expectedResult: Current data state is documented for comparison

steps.action: Using a second browser session or Postman, create a new record via the API or through the application
steps.expectedResult: A new record is successfully created in the backend

steps.action: Return to the first browser session and click a 'Refresh' button or wait for auto-refresh interval (if applicable)
steps.expectedResult: The UI component updates to show the newly created record. The record count increases by one. If real-time updates are supported, the new record appears automatically without manual refresh

steps.action: Using the second session, update an existing record's value
steps.expectedResult: The record is updated in the backend

steps.action: Refresh or wait for the first session to update and verify the changed value
steps.expectedResult: The updated value is reflected in the UI component without requiring a full page reload

postconditions: UI components accurately reflect the current state of backend data
No stale data is displayed after refresh operations
Data synchronization between frontend and backend is verified

functional.title: Verify pagination component works correctly with large datasets
preconditions: User is logged in and on a page with a paginated data table/list
Backend contains at least 50 records to enable multiple pages
Default page size is set (e.g., 10 or 25 records per page)

steps.action: Observe the pagination controls at the bottom of the data table
steps.expectedResult: Pagination controls are visible showing current page (1), total pages, and navigation buttons (Previous, Next, page numbers). The 'Previous' button is disabled on the first page

steps.action: Click the 'Next' button or page number '2'
steps.expectedResult: The table updates to show the second page of records. The page indicator updates to show page 2. The 'Previous' button becomes enabled

steps.action: Click the last page number in the pagination
steps.expectedResult: The table shows the last page of records. The 'Next' button is disabled. The record count on the last page may be less than the page size

steps.action: Change the page size selector (e.g., from 10 to 25 records per page)
steps.expectedResult: The table reloads showing 25 records per page. The total number of pages decreases accordingly. The user is returned to page 1

steps.action: Click the 'Previous' button from page 2
steps.expectedResult: The table navigates back to page 1 with the correct records displayed

postconditions: All pages display the correct number of records based on page size
Total record count remains consistent across pagination actions
No duplicate records appear across different pages

functional.title: Verify notification and toast message components display correctly for user actions
preconditions: User is logged in with permissions to perform CRUD operations
User is on a page where actions trigger notifications (e.g., form submission, record deletion)
No existing notifications are displayed on the screen

steps.action: Perform a successful action such as saving a new record by filling out a form and clicking 'Save'
steps.expectedResult: A success toast notification appears (typically green) with a message like 'Record saved successfully'. The toast appears at the top-right or top-center of the screen

steps.action: Wait for the toast notification to auto-dismiss (typically 3-5 seconds)
steps.expectedResult: The toast notification fades out or slides away automatically after the configured duration

steps.action: Perform another successful action and immediately click the 'X' close button on the toast notification
steps.expectedResult: The toast notification is dismissed immediately upon clicking the close button, before the auto-dismiss timer expires

steps.action: Trigger a warning scenario (e.g., attempt to navigate away from an unsaved form)
steps.expectedResult: A warning notification or confirmation dialog appears (typically yellow/amber) with a message like 'You have unsaved changes. Are you sure you want to leave?'

steps.action: Perform multiple rapid actions that each trigger notifications
steps.expectedResult: Multiple toast notifications stack vertically without overlapping. Each notification is independently dismissible and auto-dismisses on its own timer

postconditions: All notifications displayed with correct type (success/warning/error) and appropriate colors
Notifications did not block user interaction with the underlying page
No notification remained permanently stuck on screen

negative.title: Verify form validation rejects empty required fields on submission
preconditions: User is logged in and on a page with a form containing required fields
All form fields are empty (no pre-populated data)
The 'Submit' or 'Save' button is visible

steps.action: Without entering any data, click the 'Submit' or 'Save' button
steps.expectedResult: The form is NOT submitted. Validation error messages appear next to each required field (e.g., 'This field is required' in red text). The 'Submit' button may remain enabled but the form submission is blocked

steps.action: Observe the visual indicators on required fields
steps.expectedResult: Required fields are highlighted with red borders or red error icons. Error messages are displayed directly below or beside each empty required field

steps.action: Check the browser Network tab for any API calls
steps.expectedResult: No API call was made to the backend. The validation was performed entirely on the client side

steps.action: Fill in one required field with valid data and click 'Submit' again, leaving other required fields empty
steps.expectedResult: The filled field no longer shows an error, but the remaining empty required fields still display validation errors. The form is still not submitted

steps.action: Verify that focus is moved to the first field with a validation error
steps.expectedResult: The cursor/focus jumps to the first required field that has an error, or the page scrolls to make the first error visible

postconditions: No data was submitted to the backend
All validation error messages are clearly visible and descriptive
Form remains in its current state with user-entered data preserved in filled fields

negative.title: Verify form fields reject invalid input formats (special characters, SQL injection, XSS)
preconditions: User is logged in and on a page with a form containing text input fields
Form fields have defined input validation rules
Backend API has input sanitization enabled

steps.action: Enter a SQL injection string in a text field: ' OR '1'='1'; DROP TABLE users; --
steps.expectedResult: The input is either rejected with a validation error message (e.g., 'Invalid characters detected') or the input is accepted but sanitized. No SQL execution occurs on the backend

steps.action: Enter an XSS attack string in a text field: <script>alert('XSS')</script>
steps.expectedResult: The input is either rejected with a validation error, or if accepted, the script tags are escaped/sanitized and rendered as plain text. No JavaScript alert dialog appears

steps.action: Enter HTML injection in a text field:
steps.expectedResult: The HTML is escaped and displayed as plain text. No image element is rendered and no JavaScript executes

steps.action: Enter excessively long text (e.g., paste 10,000 characters) into a field with a character limit
steps.expectedResult: The field either truncates the input at the maximum allowed length, or displays a validation error such as 'Maximum 255 characters allowed'. A character counter may show the limit

steps.action: Enter only whitespace characters (spaces, tabs) in a required text field and submit
steps.expectedResult: The form treats whitespace-only input as empty and displays a validation error for the required field

steps.action: Submit the form and check the API request payload in the Network tab
steps.expectedResult: If the form was submitted, the payload shows sanitized/escaped values. No raw script tags or SQL commands are present in the request body

postconditions: No malicious code was executed in the browser or on the server
All dangerous input was properly sanitized or rejected
Application remains functional and secure after attempted attacks

negative.title: Verify UI handles API server errors (500 Internal Server Error) gracefully
preconditions: User is logged in and on a page that makes API calls
Backend API can be configured to return 500 errors (via mock, feature flag, or by stopping a dependent service)
Browser DevTools Network tab is open

steps.action: Configure the backend to return a 500 Internal Server Error for the next API call (or use browser DevTools to block the API endpoint)
steps.expectedResult: The API endpoint is configured to fail

steps.action: Trigger an action that makes an API call (e.g., navigate to a data page or submit a form)
steps.expectedResult: The UI displays a user-friendly error message such as 'Something went wrong. Please try again later.' instead of showing raw error details, stack traces, or a blank page

steps.action: Verify that no sensitive error information is exposed in the UI
steps.expectedResult: No stack traces, server paths, database names, or internal error codes are visible to the user. Only a generic, user-friendly error message is shown

steps.action: Check if a 'Retry' button is available and click it
steps.expectedResult: If a 'Retry' button is present, clicking it re-attempts the failed API call. If the server is still returning errors, the same user-friendly error message is displayed again

steps.action: Restore the backend to normal operation and click 'Retry' or refresh the page
steps.expectedResult: The page loads successfully with data displayed correctly. The error message disappears and normal functionality is restored

postconditions: User was never exposed to raw technical error details
Application recovered gracefully once the server error was resolved
No data corruption occurred due to the server error

negative.title: Verify UI handles network disconnection and timeout scenarios
preconditions: User is logged in and on a page with data loaded
Browser DevTools is open with ability to simulate offline mode
User has unsaved work or is about to perform an action

steps.action: In browser DevTools Network tab, check the 'Offline' checkbox to simulate network disconnection
steps.expectedResult: The browser is now in offline mode

steps.action: Attempt to perform an action that requires an API call (e.g., click 'Save' on a form)
steps.expectedResult: The UI displays a network error message such as 'No internet connection. Please check your network and try again.' The action is not completed. A visual indicator (e.g., offline banner) may appear

steps.action: Attempt to navigate to a different page within the application
steps.expectedResult: If the page requires API data, an error or offline message is displayed. If the page is cached/available offline, it loads from cache with a warning about stale data

steps.action: Uncheck the 'Offline' checkbox to restore network connectivity
steps.expectedResult: Network connectivity is restored

steps.action: Retry the previously failed action (click 'Save' again or refresh the page)
steps.expectedResult: The action completes successfully. Data is saved/loaded correctly. Any offline indicators are removed. Previously entered form data is preserved and submitted

steps.action: Set network throttling to 'Slow 3G' and trigger an API call that may timeout
steps.expectedResult: If the request times out, a timeout error message is displayed (e.g., 'Request timed out. Please try again.'). The UI does not hang or become unresponsive

postconditions: No data was lost during network disconnection
Application recovered fully when network was restored
User-entered data was preserved through the offline period

negative.title: Verify UI handles expired session and authentication token expiry
preconditions: User is logged in with a valid session
Session/token expiry time is known or can be manipulated (e.g., via DevTools Application tab)
User is on a page with active data and forms

steps.action: Open browser DevTools, go to Application tab > Cookies or Local Storage, and manually delete or modify the authentication token to make it invalid
steps.expectedResult: The authentication token is now invalid/expired

steps.action: Attempt to perform an action that requires authentication (e.g., click 'Save', navigate to a protected page)
steps.expectedResult: The API returns a 401 Unauthorized response. The UI displays a session expiry message such as 'Your session has expired. Please log in again.'

steps.action: Verify the user is redirected to the login page
steps.expectedResult: The application redirects the user to the login page automatically, or displays a modal with a 'Log In' button. The protected content is no longer accessible

steps.action: Log in again with valid credentials
steps.expectedResult: The user is authenticated successfully and redirected to the main application page or the page they were previously on

steps.action: Verify that no sensitive data from the previous session is leaked or cached inappropriately
steps.expectedResult: The new session starts fresh. If the user was redirected back to their previous page, data is re-fetched from the API with the new valid token

postconditions: Expired session was handled securely without exposing protected data
User was able to re-authenticate and resume work
No stale authentication tokens remain in browser storage

negative.title: Verify form fields reject invalid data types (letters in numeric fields, invalid email format, invalid dates)
preconditions: User is logged in and on a page with a form containing typed fields (numeric, email, date, phone)
Form validation rules are active for each field type
All fields are currently empty

steps.action: Enter alphabetic text 'abcdef' in a numeric-only field (e.g., 'Quantity', 'Amount', or 'Phone Number')
steps.expectedResult: The field either prevents non-numeric input from being typed, or displays a validation error such as 'Please enter a valid number'

steps.action: Enter an invalid email format 'notanemail@' in an email field
steps.expectedResult: A validation error appears: 'Please enter a valid email address'. The field is highlighted with a red border

steps.action: Enter another invalid email format 'user@.com' in the email field
steps.expectedResult: The same validation error appears, rejecting the malformed email domain

steps.action: Enter an invalid date '13/32/2024' (invalid month and day) in a date field, or type it manually if the date picker allows text input
steps.expectedResult: A validation error appears: 'Please enter a valid date'. The date picker does not accept the invalid date

steps.action: Enter a negative number '-5' in a field that only accepts positive values (e.g., 'Quantity')
steps.expectedResult: A validation error appears: 'Value must be greater than 0' or the field prevents negative input

steps.action: Enter '0' in a field that requires a minimum value of 1
steps.expectedResult: A validation error appears indicating the minimum allowed value

steps.action: Attempt to submit the form with all invalid values
steps.expectedResult: The form is not submitted. All validation errors remain visible. No API call is made to the backend

postconditions: No invalid data was submitted to the backend
All validation messages are specific and helpful for each field type
Form retains the invalid values so the user can correct them

negative.title: Verify UI handles API returning empty or malformed JSON responses
preconditions: User is logged in and on a page that displays API data
Backend API can be mocked to return malformed responses
Browser DevTools is open for monitoring

steps.action: Configure the API mock to return an empty response body with a 200 status code
steps.expectedResult: The UI handles the empty response gracefully, displaying an empty state message such as 'No data available' rather than crashing or showing a blank page

steps.action: Configure the API mock to return malformed JSON (e.g., '{invalid json}')
steps.expectedResult: The UI catches the JSON parse error and displays a user-friendly error message. No unhandled exception or white screen of death occurs

steps.action: Configure the API mock to return a valid JSON but with unexpected data structure (e.g., array instead of object, missing required fields)
steps.expectedResult: The UI handles the unexpected structure gracefully, either showing default/fallback values or displaying an appropriate error message. No undefined errors or broken layouts

steps.action: Configure the API mock to return null values for fields that the UI expects to be non-null
steps.expectedResult: The UI displays fallback text (e.g., 'N/A', '-', or empty string) for null values instead of showing 'null' or 'undefined' as text

steps.action: Check the browser console for any unhandled JavaScript errors
steps.expectedResult: No unhandled exceptions or uncaught promise rejections appear in the console. All errors are caught and handled gracefully

postconditions: Application remained stable and functional despite malformed API responses
No sensitive error information was exposed to the user
UI components degraded gracefully with appropriate fallback displays

negative.title: Verify concurrent/duplicate form submissions are prevented
preconditions: User is logged in and on a page with a form ready for submission
All required fields are filled with valid data
Network can be throttled to slow down API response time

steps.action: Set network throttling to 'Slow 3G' in DevTools to slow down the API response
steps.expectedResult: Network throttling is applied

steps.action: Click the 'Submit' or 'Save' button

steps.action: Run an automated accessibility audit using axe DevTools or WAVE browser extension on the full page
steps.expectedResult: No color contrast violations are reported; all text meets WCAG 2.1 AA minimum contrast ratios (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text 18px+ or 14px+ bold)

steps.action: Manually inspect body text, headings, and paragraph text using the Colour Contrast Analyser tool by sampling foreground and background colors
steps.expectedResult: All body text (under 18px) has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1; all large text (18px+ or 14px+ bold) has a contrast ratio of at least 3:1

steps.action: Inspect interactive elements (buttons, links, form inputs) for their contrast against adjacent colors in all states: default, hover, focus, active, disabled
steps.expectedResult: All interactive element boundaries and text meet a minimum 3:1 contrast ratio against adjacent colors per WCAG 2.1 AA non-text contrast requirements

steps.action: Inspect form field borders and placeholder text for contrast compliance
steps.expectedResult: Form field borders have at least 3:1 contrast against the background; placeholder text has at least 4.5:1 contrast (or is not relied upon as the only label)

steps.action: Verify that no information is conveyed by color alone (e.g., error states, status indicators, required fields)
steps.expectedResult: All color-coded information has an additional non-color indicator: icons, text labels, patterns, or underlines (e.g., error fields have both red color AND an error icon/text message)

steps.action: If dark mode is available, switch to dark mode and repeat steps 1-5
steps.expectedResult: All contrast requirements are met in dark mode as well; no text becomes invisible or hard to read against dark backgrounds

postconditions: All text content meets WCAG 2.1 AA contrast requirements
All interactive elements meet non-text contrast requirements
No information is conveyed by color alone
Both light and dark modes (if applicable) pass contrast checks

accessibility.title: Verify UI components are usable at 200% text zoom and browser zoom
preconditions: User is logged in and on the page with integrated UI components
Browser is set to default zoom (100%) and default text size
Operating system text scaling is set to 100% (default)

steps.action: Increase browser zoom to 200% using Ctrl++ (Cmd++ on Mac)
steps.expectedResult: All UI components reflow to fit the viewport; text is larger and readable; no content is cut off or hidden; no horizontal scrollbar appears on the main content area (single-column reflow is acceptable)

steps.action: At 200% zoom, verify all text content is readable and not truncated
steps.expectedResult: No text is clipped by container boundaries; text that was previously truncated with ellipsis now either wraps or can be accessed via scrolling within its container

steps.action: At 200% zoom, attempt to complete a primary user workflow (e.g., fill out a form, navigate between pages, interact with a table)
steps.expectedResult: The entire workflow is completable; all form fields are visible and fillable; all buttons are clickable; navigation works correctly

steps.action: Change only the browser's text size to 200% (in Firefox: Settings > Language and Appearance > Fonts > Size, or use 'text-only zoom' in about:config)
steps.expectedResult: Text scales to 200% while images and layout containers maintain their size; text does not overflow containers in a way that makes it unreadable; no text overlaps other text

steps.action: At 200% text zoom, verify that interactive elements maintain adequate touch/click target sizes
steps.expectedResult: All buttons and interactive elements remain at least 44x44 CSS pixels in size; elements do not overlap each other; spacing between interactive elements prevents accidental activation of adjacent elements

steps.action: Verify that no content or functionality is lost at 200% zoom by comparing with the 100% zoom view
steps.expectedResult: All content visible at 100% is accessible at 200% (via scrolling if necessary); no features are hidden or disabled due to zoom level; tooltips and popovers still appear correctly

postconditions: All content and functionality is accessible at 200% zoom per WCAG 1.4.4 (Resize Text)
No horizontal scrolling required for single-column content at 200% zoom per WCAG 1.4.10 (Reflow)
Text remains readable and does not overlap at increased sizes
All interactive elements remain usable at increased zoom levels

accessibility.title: Verify ARIA attributes are correctly implemented on custom UI components
preconditions: User is on the page with integrated UI components
Browser developer tools are open (Elements/Inspector tab)
Screen reader is active (NVDA, VoiceOver, or JAWS)
Page contains custom components (custom dropdowns, tabs, accordions, sliders, or toggle switches)

steps.action: Inspect a custom dropdown/select component in the DOM and verify its ARIA attributes
steps.expectedResult: The dropdown trigger has role="combobox" or role="listbox" with aria-expanded="false" (when closed) and aria-haspopup="listbox"; the dropdown list has role="listbox" and each option has role="option"

steps.action: Open the custom dropdown and inspect the ARIA state changes
steps.expectedResult: aria-expanded changes to "true" when opened; the active/selected option has aria-selected="true"; aria-activedescendant points to the currently highlighted option's ID

steps.action: Inspect a custom tab component and verify its ARIA attributes
steps.expectedResult: The tab list container has role="tablist"; each tab has role="tab" with aria-selected="true" for the active tab and aria-selected="false" for inactive tabs; each tab panel has role="tabpanel" with aria-labelledby pointing to its corresponding tab

steps.action: Navigate the custom tabs using Arrow keys (Left/Right for horizontal tabs, Up/Down for vertical tabs)
steps.expectedResult: Arrow keys move focus between tabs; the newly focused tab becomes active (or activates on Enter/Space depending on implementation); the corresponding tab panel content updates

steps.action: Inspect any toggle/switch components for proper ARIA implementation
steps.expectedResult: Toggle has role="switch" with aria-checked="true" or "false" reflecting its state; it has an accessible label via aria-label or aria-labelledby; state changes are announced by the screen reader when toggled

steps.action: Inspect any accordion components for proper ARIA implementation
steps.expectedResult: Accordion headers have role="button" (or are <button> elements) with aria-expanded="true" or "false"; accordion panels have role="region" with aria-labelledby pointing to their header; only expanded panels are visible in the accessibility tree

steps.action: Run axe DevTools or Lighthouse accessibility audit and check for ARIA-related violations
steps.expectedResult: No ARIA-related violations reported; no 'required ARIA attributes missing', 'ARIA roles used incorrectly', or 'ARIA hidden element contains focusable elements' errors

postconditions: All custom components have correct ARIA roles, states, and properties
ARIA states update dynamically as components change state
Screen reader announces component types, states, and changes correctly
No ARIA violations detected by automated accessibility tools

accessibility.title: Verify error messages and form validation are accessible to screen readers
preconditions: User is logged in and on a page containing a form with validation rules (required fields, format validation, etc.)
Screen reader is active (NVDA, VoiceOver, or JAWS)
Form fields are empty or in their default state
The form has at least one required field and one field with format validation (e.g., email)

steps.action: Tab to the form's submit button without filling in any required fields and press Enter
steps.expectedResult: Validation errors appear for all required fields; the screen reader announces the error summary or the first error message (e.g., 'Error: 3 fields require attention' or 'Email address is required')

steps.action: Verify that focus moves to the first field with an error or to an error summary at the top of the form
steps.expectedResult: Focus is programmatically moved to either the error summary region (with role="alert" or aria-live="assertive") or to the first invalid form field

steps.action: Navigate to each form field with an error using Tab and listen to the screen reader announcement
steps.expectedResult: Each invalid field is announced with its label, its type, AND its error message (e.g., 'Email address, edit text, required, Error: Please enter a valid email address'); the field has aria-invalid="true" and aria-describedby pointing to the error message element

steps.action: Enter an invalid email format (e.g., 'notanemail') in the email field and Tab away or trigger inline validation
steps.expectedResult: An inline error message appears (e.g., 'Please enter a valid email address'); the screen reader announces the error via aria-live region or when the field is re-focused; the error message is visually associated with the field

steps.action: Correct the email field to a valid format (e.g., 'user@example.com') and Tab away
steps.expectedResult: The error message disappears; aria-invalid is removed or set to "false"; the screen reader does not continue to announce the old error; optionally a success indicator is announced

steps.action: Fill in all required fields correctly and submit the form
steps.expectedResult: A success message is announced by the screen reader (e.g., 'Form submitted successfully') via an aria-live region; focus moves to an appropriate location (success message, next page, or top of form)

postconditions: All error messages are programmatically associated with their form fields via aria-describedby
Error states are conveyed via aria-invalid attribute on invalid fields
Dynamic error/success messages are announced by screen readers via ARIA live regions
Focus management guides the user to errors and success states appropriately

accessibility.title: Verify mobile accessibility with touch targets and gesture support
preconditions: The application is accessed on a mobile device (iOS Safari or Android Chrome) or via browser DevTools mobile emulation
User is logged in and on the page with integrated UI components
Device accessibility features are available (VoiceOver on iOS, TalkBack on Android)
Screen orientation is set to portrait mode

steps.action: Inspect all interactive elements (buttons, links, form inputs, checkboxes, toggles) for touch target size
steps.expectedResult: All interactive elements have a minimum touch target size of 44x44 CSS pixels per WCAG 2.5.5 (Target Size); elements that are smaller have sufficient spacing (at least 24px) from adjacent targets

steps.action: Attempt to tap each interactive element with a finger (or simulated touch in DevTools)
steps.expectedResult: Each element is easily tappable without accidentally activating adjacent elements; no precision tapping required

steps.action: Enable VoiceOver (iOS) or TalkBack (Android) and swipe right to navigate through all elements on the page
steps.expectedResult: The mobile screen reader navigates through all elements in a logical order; each element is announced with its label, role, and state

steps.action: With the mobile screen reader active, double-tap to activate buttons and links
steps.expectedResult: All interactive elements respond to the double-tap gesture; the expected action is performed (navigation, form submission, toggle state change)

steps.action: Rotate the device to landscape orientation and verify all UI components adapt
steps.expectedResult: All components reflow to landscape layout; no content is cut off or inaccessible; touch targets remain adequately sized; the page does not force portrait-only orientation (WCAG 1.3.4 Orientation)

steps.action: Test pinch-to-zoom on the page
steps.expectedResult: Pinch-to-zoom is not disabled (no maximum-scale=1 or user-scalable=no in the viewport meta tag); the user can zoom in to at least 200% to read content more easily

postconditions: All touch targets meet minimum size requirements
Mobile screen readers can navigate and interact with all components
Page works in both portrait and landscape orientations
Pinch-to-zoom is not restricted, allowing users to magnify content

accessibility.title: Verify visible focus indicators meet WCAG requirements on all interactive elements
preconditions: User is logged in and on the page with integrated UI components
Browser default focus styles have not been overridden to be invisible (outline: none without replacement)
Keyboard is the primary input method
Browser is Chrome, Firefox, or Edge (latest version)

steps.action: Press Tab to move focus to the first interactive element on the page and visually inspect the focus indicator
steps.expectedResult: A clearly visible focus indicator is present; it has a minimum 2px solid outline or equivalent visual treatment; the focus indicator has at least 3:1 contrast ratio against the adjacent background colors

steps.action: Continue tabbing through all interactive elements (buttons, links, inputs, checkboxes, radio buttons, dropdowns, tabs) and inspect each focus indicator
steps.expectedResult: Every interactive element displays a visible focus indicator when focused; no element has focus without a visible indicator; the indicator style is consistent across similar element types

steps.action: Tab to a button with a colored background (e.g., a primary blue button) and inspect the focus indicator visibility
steps.expectedResult: The focus indicator is visible against the button's background color; it is not obscured by the button's own styling; the indicator extends outside the button boundary or uses an inset style with sufficient contrast

steps.action: Tab to elements within a dark-themed section (if applicable) and inspect focus indicator visibility
steps.expectedResult: Focus indicators are visible against dark backgrounds; they use a light-colored outline or a high-contrast treatment that works on dark surfaces

steps.action: Click on an interactive element with the mouse, then press Tab to move focus to the next element
steps.expectedResult: Focus indicator appears on the next element after Tab press; the previously clicked element does not retain a distracting focus ring (focus-visible behavior is implemented to show focus only on keyboard navigation)

steps.action: Inspect the CSS of focus indicators using browser DevTools to verify they meet WCAG 2.4.11 (Focus Appearance) minimum area requirements
steps.expectedResult: Focus indicators have an area of at least a 2px perimeter around the component; the contrasting area between focused and unfocused states has at least 3:1 contrast ratio

postconditions: All interactive elements have visible focus indicators that meet WCAG 2.4.7 (Focus Visible)
Focus indicators have sufficient contrast against all background colors
Focus-visible behavior is implemented to avoid unnecessary focus rings on mouse interaction
Focus indicator styling is consistent across the application

accessibility.title: Verify skip navigation link and heading structure for efficient screen reader navigation
preconditions: User is on the page with integrated UI components
Screen reader is active (NVDA, VoiceOver, or JAWS)
Keyboard is the primary input method
Page has a header/navigation area and main content area

steps.action: Press Tab once from the top of the page (after page load or after pressing Ctrl+Home)
steps.expectedResult: A 'Skip to main content' link becomes visible (it may be visually hidden until focused); the screen reader announces 'Skip to main content, link'

steps.action: Press Enter on the 'Skip to main content' link
steps.expectedResult: Focus jumps to the main content area, bypassing the header and navigation; the screen reader announces the first element in the main content area; the user does not have to Tab through all navigation items

steps.action: Use the screen reader's heading navigation shortcut (H key in NVDA/JAWS browse mode, or VO+Cmd+H in VoiceOver) to navigate through all headings on the page
steps.expectedResult: Headings are announced in a logical hierarchical order: one H1 for the page title, followed by H2s for major sections, H3s for subsections, etc.; no heading levels are skipped (e.g., no H1 followed directly by H3)

steps.action: Use the screen reader's heading list feature (NVDA: Insert+F7 > Headings tab; VoiceOver: VO+U > Headings rotor) to view all headings on the page
steps.expectedResult: The heading list shows a complete and logical outline of the page content; heading text is descriptive and meaningful (not generic like 'Section 1' or empty headings)

steps.action: Verify the page has proper HTML5 semantic structure by inspecting the DOM
steps.expectedResult: The page uses semantic HTML elements: <header>, <nav>, <main>, <section>, <article>, <aside>, <footer> as appropriate; these create implicit ARIA landmarks that screen readers can navigate

steps.action: Use the screen reader's landmark navigation (D key in NVDA, or VO+U > Landmarks in VoiceOver) to jump between page regions
steps.expectedResult: Screen reader identifies distinct landmarks: banner (header), navigation, main, complementary (sidebar if present), contentinfo (footer); each landmark has a descriptive label if there are multiple of the same type (e.g., 'Primary navigation', 'Footer navigation')

postconditions: Skip navigation link is present and functional
Heading hierarchy is logical and complete with no skipped levels
Page landmarks are properly defined and labeled
Screen reader users can efficiently navigate the page structure without traversing every element sequentially
